effect: Amending a law no longer restores its full approval effect. The game fades each changed law's approval effect as voters get used to it: habituation h (0-1, per law, lawHabituation) grows 2.3% of the gap each month while the law differs from its day-0 setting (hEQ), and the law's weight in approval is importance x (1 - h) (j8). The original commit ($Lg) deleted h whenever a law changed, so a tiny amendment to a popular law gave back its full effect. Now a commit keeps h x max(0, 1 - |position change| / 100), where the position is the game's own 0-100 law score (PQ, the scale it uses for debate length and for each law's move in j8): a 5-point amendment keeps 95% of the habituation, a 50-point reform keeps half, a full swing keeps none. h is still cleared, as before, when the law returns to its day-0 setting (the monthly pass would clear it anyway) or moves across its day-0 position (a change in the other direction is new to voters). A law changed for the first time has no habituation, so it behaves as in the original game. The adoption preview (KwA, used by the law screen's forecast and per-group effects) applies the same rule, so the shown approval change matches what happens. Applies to every country, AI included. Real-world behaviour: people stay used to a policy through small amendments; only a large change feels new. No new state (lawHabituation is already saved). Day 0 unchanged: no law has habituation until the first month ends. (Minified names in this text are those of build 26318758.)
